item.title: Short AI Use Reduces Focus and Persistence, New Study Shows
item.description:
Short AI Use Reduces Focus and Persistence, New Study Shows

A peer‑reviewed study presented this week at the Conference on Language Modeling found that just ten minutes of AI assistance can significantly impair people’s ability to stay focused and persist on difficult tasks.

🔍 Overview

  • The research was led by a multinational team that includes scholars from Carnegie Mellon University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the University of Oxford, UCLA, and a research fellow with the UC Berkeley Center for Human‑Compatible AI, Brian Christian.
  • The paper builds on earlier preliminary drafts that generated media coverage from WIRED, Psychology Today, and the New York Times.

⚙️ Study Design

  • Researchers ran three randomized controlled trials with a total of 1,222 online participants.
  • Experiment 1 (354 participants): one group solved 15 basic fraction problems alone, another group solved the same problems with ChatGPT open for assistance and answer requests.
  • Experiment 2 (667 participants): a larger replication of the fraction‑problem design.
  • Experiment 3 (201 participants): participants tackled an SAT‑style reading‑comprehension prompt under the same AI‑access vs. no‑AI conditions.

📊 Key Findings

  • In the first experiment, the AI‑access group started off more accurate than the no‑AI group.
  • After participants completed 12 problems, the AI tool was removed.
  • Immediate drop: the AI‑access group’s accuracy and persistence fell sharply as soon as ChatGPT was taken away.
  • In the larger second experiment, AI users either gave wrong answers or gave up entirely when assistance was withdrawn, while the no‑AI group continued working and ended with higher success.
  • The third experiment echoed the same pattern: removal of the AI tool led to reduced persistence and accuracy on the reading task.
  • The authors conclude that short‑term reliance on AI erodes “cognitive fitness” by eliminating the “productive struggle” that helps people develop research strengths and passions.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Overreliance on AI for rapid answers can make slower, effortful problem‑solving feel inefficient.
  • Frontier AI companies acknowledge that offloading tasks to chatbots can lower baseline understanding and mastery of subjects.
  • Christian warns that in research and academia, excessive AI assistance could jeopardize core scientific habits: staying close to data, immersing in material, and collaborating in teams.
  • He suggests AI responses could default to a more instructive, tutor‑like style rather than providing instant answers.

item.title: a16z Launches Horowitz Andreessen Academy for Silicon Valley Startup Pipeline
item.description:
a16z Launches Horowitz Andreessen Academy for Silicon Valley Startup Pipeline

Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating the Horowitz Andreessen Academy, a pipeline designed for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup.

🔍 Overview

Led by a16z with $42 million in funding, the academy is described as a “highly selective school” that does not grant any accreditation or degree. It is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

🧩 How it works

The program replaces traditional academic structures with a focus on industry experience:

  • Curriculum: Short, high-impact classes led by tech figureheads, such as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
  • Practical Experience: “Co-ops” that provide students with roles at tech companies.
  • Assessment: There are no traditional grades, tests, or homework.

⚙️ Key details

Students in the program are provided with specific financial and technical resources:

  • More than $50,000 in compute credits
  • A $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z
Partner Role
Anduril Partner
Anthropic Partner
Coinbase Partner
Google Partner
Meta Partner
Nvidia Partner
OpenAI Partner
Palantir Partner
Replit Partner
Stripe Partner

🚀 Availability

  • Launch Date: The first one-year program begins in the fall of 2027.
  • Cost: The first program will be free.
  • Capacity: Only 50 students will be accepted.
  • Requirements: Students must move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing.

💡 Why it matters

The academy follows a trend of Silicon Valley billionaires, including Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos, investing in their own schools. a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges; Andreessen reportedly called the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Stanford “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with tech leaders and White House officials.

#a16z #SiliconValley #Education #Startups

Source: Andreessen Horowitz is launching an ‘academy’ with no homework and partnerships with Palantir, Google, and Meta

item.title: Tech Companies Promote AI in Schools Amid Growing Educational Scrutiny
item.description:
Tech Companies Promote AI in Schools Amid Growing Educational Scrutiny

AI companies are currently pitching schools on the necessity of generative AI, providing resources and curricula—often pro bono—to ensure students do not fall behind in a competitive job market.

💡 Why it matters

According to New York Times education technology reporter Natasha Singer, this approach mirrors how the tech industry has built influence in classrooms for 15 years. In her book Coding Kids, Singer details how companies promoted computer science as a ticket to high-paying jobs while training students on their specific software to create future customers.

⚙️ Key details

Historically, major tech companies have integrated their tools directly into educational systems:

Company Educational Tool/Method
Apple Swift curricula for AP Computer Science Principles
Microsoft Minecraft curricula for AP Computer Science Principles
Google Chromebooks and the Classroom app
Code.org “Hour of Code” campaign and celebrity-led videos

🔍 Current Status

While AI companies continue their push, several developments indicate increasing pushback:

  • School Bans: New York City has banned AI use in elementary and middle schools for the coming year, and Los Angeles has implemented broader restrictions including high schoolers.
  • Hardware Shifts: Some schools are removing Google Chromebooks.
  • Academic Findings: Global research indicates that adding technology to the classroom often does not have a significant impact on actual learning.
  • Graduate Feedback: Some recent graduates report feeling let down after being told to code their whole lives, only to find diminishing entry-level jobs.

#AI #Education #EdTech #ComputerScience

Source: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook

item.title: Microsoft agrees to enforceable AI privacy and safety principles for school districts
item.description:
Microsoft agrees to enforceable AI privacy and safety principles for school districts

Microsoft has reached a new agreement regarding AI privacy and safety rules for schools, establishing legally enforceable principles for districts that adopt them. The commitment follows a week after major school systems in New York City and Los Angeles implemented one-year bans on student-facing AI tools to allow time to establish proper guardrails.

🔍 Overview

Microsoft entered into this agreement with the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) and its New York City affiliate, the United Federation of Teachers (UFT). The terms include ten principles that school districts can choose to add to their contracts. AFT President Randi Weingarten described the terms as “iron-clad” and necessary because “no one else, including the federal government, has stepped up to do the real work.”

⚙️ Key details

The agreement establishes specific data protections and operational requirements for Microsoft’s AI tools in educational settings:

Principle Requirement
Model Training No training of AI models on student or educator data
Data Collection Limits the initial amount of data Microsoft collects
Transparency Disclosing how tools work to families in plain language
AI Companions Prohibits the use of AI companions
Risk Management Requires human review for “high-risk” decisions

💡 Why it matters

As some parents and educators resist the use of screens and AI in schools, Microsoft is responding to a policy crackdown. The AFT has been critical of tech in schools, with President Weingarten previously calling for a ban on screens before third grade and student-facing AI before middle school. However, the organization is also working with tech companies, including a $23 million AI training hub for educators funded by Anthropic, Microsoft, and OpenAI.

🚀 Availability

Starting in November, school districts can opt to add these new terms to existing or new agreements. The process is designed so districts do not have to renegotiate their entire contracts to include these protections.

#Microsoft #EdTech #AFT #AIPrivacy #Education

Source: Microsoft has new AI privacy rules for schools
